sentences.text: Shri Manish Datt - Sr. Advocate with Shri Shubham Mishra
for the appellants.

Ms. Shikha Baghel - Panel Lawyer for respondent.
I.A. No.18407 of 2025 is the repeat bail application under Section 430 (1) of Bnss, 2023/Section
389 (1) of Cr.P.C. for suspension of sentence and grant of bail on behalf of appellant No.2 Mandeep
Singh.

This Criminal Appeal assails the judgment dated 21.11.2022 passed by the learned 2nd Additional Sessions Judge, District Sagar (M.P.) in S.T. No.3900435/2016, whereby the appellant has been convicted under Sections 420 r/w 120B, 467 r/w 120B, 467 r/w 120B, 471 r/w 120B of IPC and sentenced as mentioned therein.
It is submitted by learned counsel for the present appellant No.2 Mandeep Singh that the present appellant is innocent and falsely implicated in this case.
He has served actual jail sentence of 3 years 10 months and 28 days as per the custody report dated 23.3.2026.
It is also submitted that as per the story of prosecution, present appellants have on the basis of the forged document has obtained the appointment in the Army.

That document has been seized from the possession of present appellant but that document has been supplied by co-accused Giriraj to him and Giriraj has been 2 CRA-85-2023 subsequently implicated in this case as an accused and trial has been proceeded further but by the impugned judgment Giriraj has been acquitted by the learned trial Court on the basis that no sufficient evidence has been adduced by the prosecution against co-accused Giriraj.
The investigating officer has committed grave mistake in not collecting the evidence against him.
It is also submitted that therefore, the present appellant Mandeep Singh has been convicted with the aid of Section 120B of IPC.

In these circumstances present appellant may be held responsible for taking advantage of the forged document but the forgery was actually done by co- accused Giriraj,
who has been acquitted.
Keeping in view the aforesaid circumstances and the period of incarceration, he may be released on bail during pendency of this appeal.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the prayer made by the appellant.
Heard learned counsel for the rival parties and perused the record.

sentences.text: Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, but without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I.A. No.18407 of 2025 is allowed.

It is directed that subject to depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited, and on furnishing a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with a solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court, the remaining jail sentence of the present appellant Mandeep Singh shall remain suspended and he shall be released on bail.

The 3 CRA-85-2023 present appellant is further directed to mark his appearance before the concerned Trial Court on 03.08.2026 and on subsequent dates as may be fixed by the trial Court in this regard.
List this case for final hearing in due course.
